rationale: M49/M37 #866: a FIELD member declared inside an anonymous class body (new Runnable() { int field = target(); }) is a symbol owned by the ANONYMOUS type, and the call made from its initialiser is attributed to that type. java already honoured this (it is the reference for the family convention); the fixture is added so the contract is pinned for the language that defines it, not only for the two that violated it. The `local` control pins the OTHER half of the same boundary: a method-local is not a project symbol, so a future fix that widened the boundary past the anonymous body is caught here. Call lines are pinned because the `local` call in build() is legitimately attributed to build — without the line pin a forbid on `build -> target` could never pass.

expectSymbols.name: field
expectSymbols.comment: #866 contract 1: the anon body's field is a symbol owned by the anon type

forbidSymbols.name: local
forbidSymbols.comment: #866 control: a method-local is not a project symbol

expectRelationships.comment: #866 contract 2: the initialiser call belongs to the anon type, at the call's own line
control: the method-LOCAL's call IS attributed to build

forbidRelationships.comment: the field initialiser's call must NOT flatten onto the enclosing method
JD18 leak direction: members of an anonymous body never attribute to the enclosing type
